subject: Discovery recap & next steps — Reranking model validation

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Discovery recap & next steps — Reranking model validation

Thanks for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

1) What we learned from the call
- Primary use case: session-level reranking for search and recommendation ranking (recall + reorder).
- Target latency: 75–150ms P95 for 99th percentile of queries in the US region.
- Typical request size: single query + top-20 candidate pool.
- Traffic profile: 1M requests/day expected during pilot, with seasonal spikes.
- Privacy: Acme will send anonymized query+candidate IDs; no PII in payload.

2) Proposed model candidates to evaluate
- rerank-small-v1 (distilled reranker, 1B params, optimized for latency)
- rerank-large-v2 (cross-encoder style, 7B params, higher quality/CPU)
- fallback: redwood/llama2-13b-q4 for edge cases where we need robust generalization

3) Evaluation plan / benchmarks we’ll run
- Metrics: NDCG@10, MRR@10, latency P50/P95, token cost/unit, inference error rate
- Baseline: your current production scoring (please confirm latest NDCG/MRR numbers if available)
- We'll run: offline eval on your labeled holdout, plus a small online A/B canary (5% traffic) if offline looks good

4) Deliverables and timeline
- I’ll share a draft eval report and prompt set today. Neha (ML) will validate the offline NDCG/MRR numbers and propose an A/B test plan. (Target: results within 48–72 hours of us receiving the anonymized dataset.)
- If pilot looks good, we’ll schedule a 2-week canary with a 5% traffic split, then expand to 25%+ if quality holds.

Attachments: acme_prompt_set_v1.csv (sample prompts / labels), eval_report_draft.pdf (initial offline run)

Ask: please confirm the baseline NDCG/MRR you’re targeting and grant access to the anonymized dataset or share a link to the sample file. Also confirm the PO/contract cadence so we can align pilot timing.

Thanks — looking forward to this.

Best,
Marissa

Quick internal validation results (ran on the anonymized holdout Acme uploaded):

Summary numbers (offline eval, holdout N=12,000):
- Baseline (Acme prod): NDCG@10 = 0.480 (95% CI: 0.472–0.488), MRR@10 = 0.360 (95% CI: 0.354–0.366)
- rerank-small-v1: NDCG@10 = 0.502 (95% CI: 0.494–0.510), MRR@10 = 0.372 (95% CI: 0.366–0.378)
- rerank-large-v2: NDCG@10 = 0.517 (95% CI: 0.509–0.525), MRR@10 = 0.385 (95% CI: 0.379–0.391)

Notes:
- Both candidates show statistically significant improvements vs baseline (bootstrap test, p < 0.01). Absolute deltas: +0.022 and +0.037 for NDCG@10.
- Latency estimates (P95): rerank-small-v1 ~ 62ms (g4dn), rerank-large-v2 ~ 128ms (g4dn). Hosted estimates similar with q4 quantization: small ~55ms, large ~110–140ms.
- Cost: small is ~0.35x cost of large per request in our test harness.
- Failure modes: the large model is more robust on long-tail queries (sparse context). Small model occasionally falls back to surface-level lexical signals.

Recommendation (A/B plan):
- Canary: 5% traffic for 7 days, split 50/50 between rerank-small-v1 and rerank-large-v2 vs baseline (three-arm canary). Monitor NDCG, MRR, CTR, and latency P95.
- Stopping criteria: if either candidate underperforms baseline on NDCG by >0.01 at p<0.05 after 3 days, pause that variant.
- Ramp: if both pass, promote the better-performing model to 25% for 7 days, then gradual 50%+ split based on business KPIs.

I attached the full CSV: ndcg_mrr_results.csv (per-query NDCG/MRR, bootstrap CI). Happy to walk through specifics with Acme.

—Neha
